parsed.attack: OurFamilyWizard is the incumbent, and its distribution is a judge's order rather than a marketing budget. It already ships a timestamped Journal alongside its message and calendar records, and TalkingParents sells certified, unalterable records as its entire product; adding structured bedtime fields and dictation to an existing Journal is one release for either of them. The exported PDF is where this really loses: those companies' records are accepted because a third party certifies them, whereas a PDF generated by an app one parent installed and controls is the weakest available exhibit, and the family-law practitioners who are supposed to be the zero-budget referral loop will keep pointing clients at the mandated app for exactly that reason.
parsed.strongest_defence: OurFamilyWizard's premise is a shared, mutually discoverable record: anything written there is visible to the other party and to the court by design, which is why it cannot host one parent's private contemporaneous observations. A parent's own log, kept beside the mandated app rather than inside it, is structurally something the incumbent cannot ship without breaking the neutrality that makes it court-mandated in the first place.
parsed.verdict_reason: The incumbent already has the Journal and owns the admissibility that gives the artifact its value, but it cannot host a private one-sided record, which leaves a narrow lane the feature-ship does not close.
